more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
Approved in the US.
more_info.overview: Tartrazine is a manufactured azo dye that gives food a yellow colour. It is sold in the US as FD&C Yellow No. 5. Food-grade material is a purified salt mixture meeting colour specifications. The specified material is supplied as powder or granules.
more_info.origin: Synthetic. An aromatic sulfonic acid is diazotised, coupled to a pyrazole compound, and the dye is purified as its sodium salt.
more_info.daily_intake: 0–10 mg/kg body weight per day (JECFA, 2016). EFSA retained 7.5 mg/kg body weight per day in 2009; these are distinct assessments.
more_info.side_effects:
At food-use levels, EFSA reported intolerance reactions in a small fraction of people; reactions can occur within the ADI. Studies of colour mixtures with sodium benzoate do not establish that tartrazine alone causes behavioural changes.
At high experimental doses, reduced body weight in rats was the endpoint for JECFA's 2016 ADI. This animal evidence does not establish the same effect at food-use levels in humans.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; flavoured drinks; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products; unripened cheese excluding products falling in category 16.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.precautions: EFSA noted that sensitive individuals may react at intakes within the ADI.
